utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. We're in open session. I would first like to ask Madam Registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-00-39-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I think the Prosecution would like to know in which week we would not be sitting in November. That will be the week starting the -- I think the 13th of November is a Monday, if I'm not... 15th. Well, that week, yes, 15th up to and including the 19th, the Friday, we'll not be sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's extremely helpful to know, Your Honour. Is there any indication also at this stage of which week -- I think there's one week the Trial Chamber is considering sitting in the afternoon rather than the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I already gave the programme about morning and afternoon sessions. I haven't got it in my mind at this moment. But I delivered a schedule for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. If that's answered then, all sorts of things happen when I'm not looking, royalty visits, schedules get sorted out. My apologies for taking up time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there's no other issue at this moment to be raised, we'll turn into closed session to continue the examination of the present witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're in open session again. Ms. Loukas, I do understand that the issue to be raised is about the scheduling of the testimony of the expert witness Ms. Hansen, which was originally announced for, I think, the 21st of October. And I do understand that there have been some communication between the parties, Prosecution willing to delay -- to postpone, but not for such a time that would be agreeable for the Defence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour. And of course, in the two or three minutes I have available what I can outline is this: The Defence is simply not in a position to deal with Ms. Hansen's evidence at this time. And the one week suggestion by the Prosecution is simply not adequate to our purposes. The situation we find ourselves in, and this is something we've made clear to the Trial Chamber on a number of occasions, is that our would-be pre-trial preparation is occurring whilst the trial proceeds. And it's an invidious, untenable position. But specifically in relation to this witness, Your Honour, this is -- the evidence of this particular expert is critical, would-be linkage evidence, it relates to all the municipalities in the indictment. We're still in the process at this stage of still churning through the 92 bis submissions in relation to all the municipalities. And Your Honour, in those circumstances, I'd also go to the extent of the material. And I actually have a memo in which I can outline to Your Honours the extent of the material, but just as an example, we got a new documents disclosure this week, Tuesday, the 5th of October, a CD containing 69 documents, only two of the 69 documents have English translations. We're dealing with, Your Honour, an expert's report that refers to the -- refers to 372 different documents. We've only a quarter of the way through printing this material. We are just simply, Your Honour, not in a position to deal with this witness at this time. I can appreciate the OTP wishes, and they have the right to run their case in any way they and at what point they wish. But on the other hand from the Defence perspective, it's in the interests of justice, Your Honour, that the Defence has proper time for preparation. And we simply do not. And Your Honour, we cannot deal with this witness at this point in time. One last point in terms of my two or three minutes, is that the particular witness in question that we're dealing with doesn't present at the particular logistical exercises because the expert in question is employed by the office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber is aware of that. Mr. Hannis, please respond. And if the flexibility would be greater than appeared until now in the communications, the Chamber would like to hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would like to try to work with the Court and the Defence. However, I would note for Your Honour that this expert report was filed in July 2002. There were 331 documents mentioned in the 142 footnotes in that report that were disclosed at that time. There has been separate disclosure of all those documents in addition since then related to the various municipalities, and Mr. Treanor. This witness was first noticed as being one that we wanted to call on the 18th of October by an email that we sent to Mr. De Hemptinne and the Defence on the 10th of September. I understand there were 15 additional documents consisting of 30 pages that were disclosed on the 1st of October. However, they are not new material, Your Honour. They're more in the nature of documents that supplement the original 331. We could move the witness further on, but we have witnesses scheduled, for example, in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd of November. We have witnesses scheduled. They're planning to attend then. We might put them the week after that. But -- whatever the Court's decision is, we ask that we have that as soon as possible so we can make the logistical changes for the other witnesses that would be replaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's perhaps the wrong expression, but it one more week your last offer, or is it...? I asked you about the flexibility. And while you indicated there's still some flexibility, but you know elastic at a certain moment breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, looking at it, the following week we have two witnesses tentatively scheduled, but they're not as firm. It might be easier to put Ms. Hansen the week of November 8th, and keep the witnesses we have currently scheduled for the 1st through the 5th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour, because I think we're probably running out of tape at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said, my information about the tape is not fully correct. But this is again not an invitation.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to this, I can indicate that taking on board the scheduling aspects that have been mentioned by Mr. Hannis, it seems to be more appropriate that we deal with this particular witness at a time when we don't have a scheduling difficulty which I assume might be early next year, in which case we will have dealt with all the 92 bis submissions. We will have been through all the municipalities at that point, and it's more appropriate to call her at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber will consider what to do. Mr. Hannis, let me just very practically ask you. We'll not sit in the week -- you said now it's possible the week of the 8th of November. You know that we're not sitting in the week starting the 15th of November. So a further postponement of one week would actually be two weeks. Would that still be within your flexibility reach?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Your Honour. You're talking about postponing then until the week of the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because we'll not sit in the week of the 13th -- it's the 15th until the 19th. That means that 22nd would then be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, presently the difficulty with that week is there's a witness that we've tentatively tried to schedule for that week. That may be the only week we can get him in, in the near future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how many days would that witness take?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I consult with Mr. Harmon for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness we have proposed for that Monday and Tuesday is scheduled to take perhaps six or eight hours on direct. But we could start Ms. Hansen later in the week, Wednesday or Thursday. Your Honour, I did want to raise one other concern in light of Ms. Loukas's announcement in Court last week, I believe, or earlier this week that she proposes to file a motion of withdrawal, we have a concern about how that may impact on this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you'll understand that by postponing we try to keep Ms. Loukas on board as long as possible. Mr. Hannis, of course, as you may have noticed at that time, the Chamber has heard what Ms. Loukas said. And the Chamber finds it not appropriate to address that matter up to the moment that Ms. Loukas addresses the matter. So we'll stay out of that. Ms. Loukas, the second half of the week starting the 22nd of November. I know it's not January, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I must say from my perspective, it's quite clear that if we are to meet the 92 bis schedule set out in meetings with the representatives from the Trial Chamber, it's very difficult for me to see how we can deal with the current trial schedule at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would postponement -- well, specifically in that period, of course not postpone the whole of the 92 bis, would that contribute to -- well, let's say one or two municipalities, or postponement of one week? Of course, I have to -- I'm aware that also the 92 bis, of course, is a matter of scheduling preparation for the Chamber. Bun one thing for certain, your suggestion was to hear first all of the municipalities, the Chamber is a bit concerned about hearing all of the crime-base evidence and not to hear important evidence on the vertical issues as well. But it's certainly hearing the expert evidence of Ms. Hansen would certainly give a brief delay in further hearing crime-base evidence. So perhaps we could consider to give you some additional time at that moment to present your 92 bis positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just make one comment in relation to Your Honour's observation, and that is this: My suggestion was that it would be more appropriate to deal with this particular expert witness's evidence once we had finished the 92 bis process as opposed to necessarily hearing all the evidence from the various municipalities. And if one looks at the current 92 bis process, the week that we have out of court, next week, for example, I'm currently in the process of having all the 92 bis material printed out for the next log which is at this stage already 2.000 pages. And we have another series of that nature until the end of December, which will take up all the time that we have out of the trial schedule. I have to make that point clear, Your Honour, that we're dealing with -- from the Defence perspective, a next to impossible schedule in conjunction with the other matters that we have to take ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Combining all of the 92 bis work and dealing with Ms. Hansen would be a major problem for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, I wish we were in the luxurious position of having seven counsel as the Prosecution does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, we have discussed that many times. That counsel in court does not mean that counsel are available fulltime for that case. So let's not reiterate that. I do see that the Prosecution has showed some willingness to further postpone, and I also notice that you're still not in a position to, say, well, that is although not I wished, it is acceptable to me. If that's the situation, the Chamber will have to give it some consideration.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I come back to the issue that has been discussed in the presence of Mr. Hannis just before the break, that is, the timing of the testimony of the expert witness, Ms. Hansen. From what I understand that the Prosecution now takes the position that it could be postponed until approximately 25th, 26th of November to start with. The Chamber intends to follow approximately, so that whenever it would be the 25th of or the 26th, or the beginning of the next week which would bring us early in December to hear the testimony of Ms. Hansen at that time, but before giving a final decision, the Chamber would very much during the next week, when we're not sitting, the Chamber would very much like the parties to sit together and to rediscuss the 92 bis schedule because 92 bis was one of the -- I'm not saying it would be totally overthrown, but at least to give some relief to the Defence in view of the 92 bis schedule. And at the same time, the Chamber invites the Prosecution, having heard the number and not being fully aware yet of what it all contains, but having heard the number of the 92 bis material, to invite the Prosecution to review to what extent it's all really needed. I remember one case -- one 92 bis moment in this case where 1.050 pages were finally reduced to 6. Of course, that was a very dramatic reduction, and I'm not saying that you always can take 1 per cent and that would be enough. So therefore, the parties are invited to -- I wouldn't say renegotiate, but at least to see whether any adaptation could be made on the 92 bis schedule as agreed upon until now, preferably under the guidance of Mr. De Hemptinne because he was involved, or perhaps since he might not be there next week, Mr. Harhoff, and at the same time the Prosecution is invited to see to what extent all the huge number of 92 bis pages are really necessary, and I -- then especially, but I do not know whether there are any transcripts involved in it, because that's what usually takes the huge number of pages, rather than the statements. So it is all a bit related, so we do not give a final decision at this moment. But certainly, we'll not -- I mean, the flexibility shown by the Prosecution, will not say no, we would like to hear that evidence earlier, although the Chamber wants to have a fair balance in horizontal and vertical aspects and not to wait until the very end of the case to hear any vertical evidence, and having heard meanwhile all the evidence on all the municipalities. But whether it will be the second half of the last week of November or the first week of December is still something to be seen and could be part of the discussions perhaps between the parties as well. But we'll give a decision if there's no agreement once the Chamber restarts sitting on the 21st of October it is, I think. 22nd. Then we turn into closed session again to continue the examination of the present witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session again. Having concluded the testimony of the witness, the Chamber adjourns until the 18th of October, quarter past 2.00 in Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of October, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 16 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.52 p.m.,
